findings.message: The loop body is forward, loss, backward, step (cell 3, lines 6-10). No cell calls optimizer.zero_grad() or model.zero_grad(), or resets .grad; all four cells were read. Under PyTorch's accumulate-on-backward semantics, every step after the first applies Adam to the running sum of all earlier batches' gradients instead of the current batch's gradient. Basis is inferred because the consequence rests on framework semantics; the absence itself is read directly from the source. This is a property of cell 3 alone and does not depend on cell order. Runtime-dependent parts: (1) the effect needs more than one batch, i.e. more than 32 training rows; the row count is unknown because features.npz is not in the workspace, and with a single batch the one pass has only one step and nothing accumulates; (2) whether the loop ran at all in the recorded session is unresolved (see recorded-order-dependency). Re-running cell 3 rebuilds model and optimizer on lines 1 and 3, so accumulated gradients do not carry over between executions of the cell; the accumulation is confined to the batches of one pass.
findings.suggestion: Call optimizer.zero_grad() at the top of each iteration, before the forward pass.
findings.title: Training loop never clears gradients (no optimizer.zero_grad())

findings.message: scaler.fit_transform(X) (cell 2, line 2) runs before train_test_split(X_scaled, ...) (cell 2, lines 3-4), so the scaler's mean and scale include the 20% of rows that become X_test. Both statements sit in the same cell, so the fit-before-split order holds in source order and in any execution order in which cell 2 completes. Runtime-dependent part: which array X was bound when cell 2 ran. In source order it is the features array loaded in cell 1; in the recorded order cell 2 (count 2) precedes the load cell (count 3), so the identity of X is unresolved. Impact inside this notebook is limited: only X_train and y_train are consumed downstream and X_test / y_test are never evaluated, so no reported metric is inflated here. The held-out split is nevertheless contaminated from the moment it is created, and any evaluation later added on X_test would be optimistic. No second fit on X_train alone and no Pipeline exists in any cell.
findings.suggestion: Split first, then scaler.fit(X_train) and transform both splits with that fitted scaler, or wrap scaler and model in a Pipeline.
findings.title: StandardScaler is fit on all rows before the train/test split

findings.message: Metadata, which cell-source citations cannot quote: execution_count is 1 for cell 0, 3 for cell 1, 2 for cell 2 and 4 for cell 3, and every outputs array is empty. X and y are assigned only in cell 1 (lines 4-5), yet cell 2, which reads both (lines 2 and 4), carries the lower count. What actually happened depends on kernel state that the file does not save, so it is unresolved: (a) if the counts come from one fresh kernel, cell 2 raised NameError at fit_transform(X), X_train never existed, and cell 3 at count 4 failed at torch.tensor(X_train) (line 4), meaning no training occurred; (b) if X and y were already bound (for example counts left from different sessions, source edited after running, or a hand-written file; the list is not exhaustive), the model at count 4 was trained on a split of that earlier X, and the data re-loaded at count 3 was never scaled, split or trained on. No error output is stored, but empty outputs neither confirm nor exclude (a). In either case the saved counts do not demonstrate a successful clean-kernel run; source order is the only ordering whose data flow the source itself establishes.
findings.suggestion: Restart the kernel, run all cells top to bottom, and save only after that run completes; treat source order as canonical.
findings.title: Recorded execution counts place the scale/split cell before the cell that defines X and y
